title: Toxo'o o tsui' kiee'n: Day of the Death in the Mazatecan Highlands in Oaxaca
description: The Day of the Dead celebration in the Sierra Mazateca territory is known as ·Tsui' kiee'n· or ·The Festival of the Sun·

author.name: Cinthia Karina Baños Paredes
author.affiliation: National School of Anthropology and History (ENAH)

captions: The Cemetery Vigil: The Sea of Light. In the depths of the night of October 31st, the Mazatec community cemetery transforms into a sea of light. This image captures hundreds of burning candles illuminating the graves, creating a sacred landscape where fire symbolizes the living presence of the deceased. According to Mazatec cosmology, candlelight serves as a guide for souls to find their way back to earth during these sacred days. Families remain throughout the night in vigil, conversing with their dead, sharing food and drink, keeping candles perpetually lit.

Chaxo o': The Huehuentón as Ancestral Portal. The Huehuentón (chaxo o' in Mazatec) is much more than a masked dancer: it is the physical embodiment of ancestors returning to the world of the living. This photograph captures the ritual moment of transformation when the mask bearer ceases to be an individual and becomes a vessel for ancestral spirits. The carved wooden mask represents the face of the ancients, the "navel of the earth" who founded the community. The multicolored textile—woven by women with patterns representing the four directions of the cosmos—serves as spiritual armor protecting the bearer during transit between worlds.

The Home Altar: Architecture of Reunion. The home altar is a complex cosmological construction that functions as a dimensional portal between the realm of the living (tikjandá) and that of the dead (nda kjuani). This image shows a multi-level altar that replicates the vertical structure of the Mazatec universe: the upper level represents heaven decorated with cempasúchil flowers whose aroma guides the spirits; the middle level symbolizes the land of the living with photographs and favorite foods; the lower level represents the underworld with candles and copal that purify the path of ascent. Families construct these altars weeks in advance, and during the days of Tsui' kiee'n they maintain constant conversation with the photographs.

The Procession of Masks: Ritual Geography of the Town. The Huehuentones do not dance just anywhere: their route through the town traces a sacred geography that reactivates points of spiritual power. This photograph documents the moment when a group of fifteen Huehuentones proceeds along the main street, stopping at specific houses where community members have died during the year. At each stop, they execute a particular dance that varies according to the age and social role of the deceased. The masks they wear are inherited through generations, some more than 100 years old, accumulating the spiritual power of all the ancestors they have represented.

title: The Two Walls
description: Since 2019, Mexico's immigration policies have undergone a significant shift, transforming from a nation historically open to migrants and asylum seekers at its southern border to a country that enforces stringent immigration policies.

author.name: Alejandro Cegarra
author.profession: Documentary Photographer & Visual Journalist - The New York Times/Bloomberg

captions: Ruben Soto (right), a migrant from Venezuela, sits with Rosa Bello, a Honduran migrant, atop a freight train known as "The Beast," in Samalayuca, Mexico. Ruben and Rosa met in Mexico and fell in love on their way to the United States.

A migrant jumps between cars on a freight train known as "The Beast" in Piedras Negras, Mexico. Migrants and asylum seekers lacking the financial resources to pay a smuggler often resort to using cargo trains to reach the United States border. This mode of transportation is very dangerous; over the years, hundreds have fallen onto the tracks and have been killed or mutilated. Thousands more have fallen victim to extortion, rape, kidnapping, or robbery orchestrated by drug cartels or corrupt authorities in various stops along the train's northward route.

The De Coto family poses for a portrait aboard "The Beast" while heading to Ciudad Juárez. This photo was taken in Samalayuca, Mexico, three days before the expiration of Title 42, a US COVD-19 prevention measure that in effect allowed deportation of migrants without reviewing asylum claims. Since 2020, there have been over two million expulsions of migrants by US Customs and Border Protection under Title 42.

Ruben Soto (right), a migrant from Venezuela, sits with Rosa Bello, a Honduran migrant, atop a freight train known as "The Beast," in Samalayuca, Mexico. Ruben and Rosa met in Mexico and fell in love on their way to the United States.

title: The Lake Has Fallen Silent
description: Lake Kivu, a majestic body of water at the border between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, is a place where stories intertwine and destinies converge. Beneath the placid beauty lies turbulence and uncertainty.
captions: A fisherman repairs his nets at dawn along the shores of Lake Kivu in Goma, DRC. Against the backdrop of storm clouds and the bustling harbor, he prepares for another day on waters that have sustained his community for generations, even as climate change brings increasingly unpredictable weather patterns and declining fish populations.

Sambaza, a sardine local to the waters of Lake Kivu, are captured in a net. Several factors, including overfishing and the presence of gas extraction plants, threaten the sambaza population, in Goma, DRC.
Women selling sambaza at Rond-Point Rutshuru, a busy street in Goma, DRC.
A woman eats sambaza and fufu at a restaurant in Goma, DRC.

title: Occupy Parliament: Kenya's Finance Bill Protests
description: Documenting the nationwide protests against the Finance Bill 2024 in Kenya, where a generation of young activists took to the streets demanding accountability and rejecting punitive taxation.
captions: Protestors chant anti-government slogans while climbing a Kenya Police water cannon truck during a nationwide protest against tax hikes and the Finance Bill 2024 in Nairobi, Kenya.
Protestors chant slogans and push a makeshift barricade as they clash with Kenyan police officers during an anti-government demonstration in Nairobi, Kenya.
A Kenyan police officer fires a tear gas canister during a demonstration against tax hikes as Members of Parliament vote on the Finance Bill 2024 in downtown Nairobi, Kenya.
A tear gas canister explodes under a protestor in Nairobi, Kenya.

title: The Darién Gap: The World's Most Dangerous Migration Route
description: Visual documentation of one of the most dangerous migration routes in the world: the Darién Gap, a 100-kilometre stretch of dense jungle that connects Colombia and Panama.
captions: A group of Afghan, Chinese, Venezuelan, and Ecuadorian migrants wade toward a boat headed for the Darién Gap, in Capurganá, Colombia. Many of the Afghans had never seen the ocean before.
A final base camp before entering the Darién Gap, in Las Tecas, Colombia. A record 520,000 migrants crossed through the Darién jungle in 2023.

Thousands of migrants wade into the Rio Muerto ("Death River") at the Darién Gap, where several have drowned in its treacherous waters. They assist one another to prevent drowning in the swift currents.

Sarah Cuauro, (6) was separated from her mother during their trek through the jungle. Ángel Garcia, (42) took care of her for several days as they climbed through the mud to Banderas Hill, a crossing point in the Darién Gap. They had no idea where Sarah's mother was or whether she was injured.

title: Cool Burning: Indigenous Fire Management in West Arnhem Land
location_name: West Arnhem Land, Northern Territory, Australia
description: Indigenous Australians have strategically burned land to protect their environment for tens of thousands of years. In a practice known as cool burning, fires move slowly, burn only the undergrowth, and remove the build-up of fuel that feeds bigger blazes.
captions: Nawarddeken women conducting traditional cool burning in West Arnhem Land. The controlled fires move slowly through the grasslands, burning only undergrowth while leaving trees intact, creating a mosaic pattern that prevents larger wildfires during the dry season.

Nawarddeken elder Conrad Maralngurra burns grass to protect the Mamadawerre community from late-season wildfires, in Mamadawerre, Arnhem Land, Australia. The late-evening fire will die out naturally once the temperature drops and moisture levels rise.
Smoke from a cool-burn fire covers Djalama Valley in West Arnhem Land, at the beginning of the dry season in Australia's Northern Territory.
Stacey Lee (11, left) sets the bark of trees alight to produce a natural light source to help hunt for file snakes (Acrochordus arafurae), in Djulkar, Arnhem Land, Australia.

title: Two Chinas on Rails
description: A photographic exploration of China's dual railway system, where gleaming high-speed trains and aging slow trains run in parallel, revealing the stark class divisions and inequalities within the world's largest rail network.
captions: At Beijing West Railway station, a migrant worker loaded with baggage, heads back to the family hometown for the New Year holiday. The Lunar New Year is the busiest time of year for train travel, with an estimated 190 million trips taken during the 2024 spring festival holidays. The modernisation of the China Railway network has made this yearly migration a lot easier, reducing it to a few hours when it could take one or two days just a decade earlier.
In the VIP waiting room of Chengdu Airport, recently opened high-speed railway station, a detail of painting shows a high-speed train riding in a mountainous landscape.

A crowded concourse at Beijing West railway station, a few days before the Lunar New Year. The station was the largest in Asia when it was inaugurated in the late 90s but it has struggled to keep up with expanding passenger numbers as China's railways undergo modernisation. It serves both green (slow) trains, and some high speed trains.

title: The Persistence of Caste Power: The Panchayats of North India
description: Twenty months of fieldwork in Jat farming villages around Sonipat, Haryana, show how caste councils (panchayats) still settle marriage disputes, shape village elections and lead the campaign for reservations, although they are often described as a thing of the past.
captions: The advancing urban frontier in a village near Sonipat city.
A Jat village chaupal, the most common site for holding the panchayat.
A village Jat panchayat.
A Jat maha-panchayat.

title: Common Practices on the Use of Public Pastures in Highland Kyrgyzstan
description: In Tamga, a village in the Kyrgyz Tian Shan, a 2009 reform made the municipality responsible for its own public pastures. This study follows the everyday work of sharing the grassland: grazing rules, maps, irrigation water and help between herding families.
captions: Rearing cattle on one of Tamga's summer pastures (djajloo), August 2015.
Kara Suu in the second year of the moratorium, August 2019.
A shepherd's syrt camp with one of the new cubic houses, Djaman Tam, August 2018.
The maps of Tamga's pasturage in the pasture committee's office, Tamga, July 2019.
